overview: This file documents Japanese censorship of international commercial cable and radio traffic in Japanese-occupied Chinese treaty ports during the first half of 1938. Cross-reference sheets and two diplomatic telegrams report requirements to disclose commercial codes or supply codebooks at Tianjin, Shanghai, and Yantai, together with protests or objections by American, British, and German interests. The correspondence emphasizes the threatened delay, exposure of confidential business information, and possible economic harm caused by censorship, while also recording attempts to preserve procedures previously used under Chinese administration.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Oppenheimer Casing Company letter on censorship at Tientsin
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a letter protesting Japanese censorship of cables and radio messages sent from Tientsin to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Oppenheimer Casing Company feared Japanese censorship of its Tientsin-U.S. communications would harm its sausage-casing import business.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Gauss telegram on coded commercial messages at Shanghai
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to telegram no. 164 concerning Japanese censorship of coded commercial messages at Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Gauss reports Japan will censor Shanghai coded commercial cables, with the chief censor open to continuing prior Chinese-censorship procedures.

subfiles.title: Gauss telegram on Japanese censorship of Shanghai commercial cables
subfiles.about: Gauss objects to Japanese censorship of American commercial code messages and describes a proposed accommodation based on earlier Chinese procedures.
subfiles.summary: Gauss tells Japan's Consul General he won't recognize a right to censor American firms' coded Shanghai cables, citing Japan's own refusal of Chinese censorship; pending settlement, censors would accept messages bearing a consular seal certifying no military content.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Roberts telegram on codebook demands at Chefoo
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a telegram reporting that Japanese authorities required Chefoo firms to supply codebooks before coded messages would be delivered.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan demanded Chefoo firms' codebooks for decoding incoming messages; British and German firms protested, no American complaint yet.

subfiles.title: Roberts telegram on Japanese codebook requirements at Chefoo
subfiles.about: Roberts reports Japanese requirements for decoding incoming private-code messages at Chefoo and the response of foreign firms.
subfiles.summary: From June 13, Japan required Chefoo firms to surrender codebooks for decoding incoming mail; British and German firms protested, but no American firm had yet complained.

interest: Shows Japanese military censorship of commercial cables in Chinese treaty ports, varying by local negotiation.
